summary:
The ACES Act of 2025 (Pub. L. 119-32, S. 201, enacted August 14, 2025) directs the commissioning of an independent epidemiological study on cancer prevalence and mortality among former active duty fixed-wing aircrew. The Act is freestanding legislation; it does not amend title 38 or other existing U.S. Code provisions.

Section 1 provides the short title. Section 2 constitutes the operative provision.

Section 2(a) directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs, not later than 30 days after enactment, to "seek to enter into" an agreement with the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine to conduct the study. This is a duty to seek an agreement rather than an unqualified mandate to execute one. Under subsection (a)(2)(A), the Secretary must finalize the agreement within 60 days after entering negotiations. Subsection (a)(2)(B) establishes a fallback reporting mechanism triggered by failure to meet the 60-day deadline: the Secretary must submit to the Senate and House Committees on Veterans' Affairs a report explaining the failure and estimating a finalization date, and must provide progress briefings to those committees not less frequently than every 60 days thereafter.

Section 2(b) prescribes the study's scope. The National Academies shall (1) identify exposures associated with covered individuals' military occupations, including chemicals, compounds, agents, and other phenomena; (2) conduct a literature review of associations between such exposures and overall cancer morbidity and mortality and the incidence/prevalence of twelve enumerated cancers (brain, colon and rectal, kidney, lung, melanoma skin, non-Hodgkin lymphoma, pancreatic, prostate, testicular, thyroid, urinary bladder), plus other cancers the Secretary designates in consultation with the National Academies; and (3) determine, to the extent possible, prevalence and mortality among covered individuals using available data sources, which may include VA, DoD, and Service administrative and health databases, the National Death Index maintained by the CDC's National Center for Health Statistics, and the study conducted under section 750 of the William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021 (Pub. L. 116-283, 134 Stat. 3716).

Section 2(c) requires the National Academies, at the study's conclusion, to submit a report of results to the Secretary and the two Veterans' Affairs Committees. No deadline is fixed for study completion or the final report.

Section 2(d) defines "covered individual" as a person who served on active duty in the Army, Navy, Air Force, or Marine Corps as a fixed-wing aircrew member—including pilot, navigator, weapons systems operator, aircraft system operator, or any other crew member who regularly flew in a fixed-wing aircraft.

The Act contains no authorization of appropriations or appropriation of funds.
